key_insight: Charge shifted through a semiconductor channel wears only gate dielectrics, dodging the write-endurance wall; one sense amp per 64 bits removes per-cell transistors, capacitors and contacts.
killer_doubt: 192 transfers need CTE >=0.9995 (imec IGZO: >98%); a 64-bit shift at imec's ~4 MHz takes ~48 us; 60 nm pitch is ~2.5x too tight (realistic ~300 nm2/bit).
decisive_experiment: Merge into the I-10793/N-08 dossier: university-fab planar 3-phase IGZO and poly-Si CCD lines of 192 gates; measure CTE versus clock (4-100 MHz) and dark fill at 85 C. Go if >=0.9995 at >=20 MHz.
prior_art: imec IEDM 2024 planar IGZO CCD (CTE >98%) and IMW 2026 vertical 3D IGZO CCD (via search snippet, logged in R16); 1970s Si CCD memories.

key_insight: Frozen weights need neither writes nor refresh, so read-only bits from a mature U.S. logic fab could offload HBM capacity without capacitors or EUV.
killer_doubt: Stacked present/absent-via decks lack per-bit selectors, so sneak paths through shorted vias defeat crosspoint reads; one deck at 64 nm pitch is ~4,100 nm2/bit, ~4x below 1b DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Do not fund separately; fold into I-03028's 28 nm MPW NOR-ROM macro and $/GB model versus HBF. A selector-less 1k x 1k via crosspoint test chip would show the sneak-path margin collapse.
prior_art: Mask ROM since the 1970s; e-beam direct-write ROM coding; Taalas hardwired-model chips (2026); I-03028 (R16). From memory, unverified.

key_insight: Size-coded vias give 2 bits per site, and re-spinning only one via mask per model keeps NRE near $0.1-0.3M on a mature node.
killer_doubt: '2-4 bits per F2' is 4-8x high: a crosspoint site is >=4F2, so 2-bit vias give 0.5 bit/F2; at F=45 nm ~4,000 nm2/bit, ~4x below 1b DRAM, before selectors.
decisive_experiment: Duplicate of I-02068; fund only inside I-03028's MPW: measure 2-bit via-size resistance distributions (4 levels) and read margin with a diode selector across 0-85 C.
prior_art: Multi-level via/implant-coded mask ROM (1990s); Taalas hardwired-model chips (2026); covered by the I-03028 dossier. From memory, unverified.

key_insight: LLM decode activates every weight row each 10-25 ms sweep, inside tREFW, so streamed rows refresh themselves; HBM dies failing the 32 ms screen could be binned for weights.
killer_doubt: Skipping REF also skips in-DRAM TRR row-hammer refresh, so PRAC/RFM is required; per-bank refresh already hides most tRFC, leaving ~5-10% bandwidth. Retention's share of HBM yield loss is unknown.
decisive_experiment: FPGA DDR4/DDR5 tester (DRAM Bender): replay LLM weight-stream traces with REF disabled plus ACT-based targeted refresh at 85 C for 30 days; log errors. Separately quantify dies rejected only by the retention screen.
prior_art: Smart Refresh (Ghosh and Lee, MICRO 2007) skips recently accessed rows; ESKIMO (MICRO 2009) skips unallocated memory; LPDDR PASR. From memory.

key_insight: Active neutralisation needs no new device: a per-bitline gain stage cancels ~50-70% of Cbl during 1-2 ns charge sharing, so Cs can fall 2-3x on today's 512-cell bitline.
killer_doubt: Stability needs Cn below capacitance to static nodes; BL-BL coupling (assume 20-30% of Cbl) follows neighbour data, so worst patterns may cap Cn/Cbl near 0.5 (2x, not 3.3x).
decisive_experiment: 28-65 nm MPW ($150-300k): 64 emulated 35 fF bitlines with 1-5 fF MIM cell stubs and per-line neutralisers; measure signal, offset and oscillation under all-0, all-1 and checkerboard data, beside N-04 charge-transfer pre-sense.
prior_art: Electrophysiology headstage capacitance neutralisation; clamped-bitline sense amp (Blalock, IEICE). No DRAM bitline neutraliser found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Compaction before self-refresh lets partial-array masks stop refresh on vacated segments; useful for phones and idle CXL pools.
killer_doubt: Saves idle refresh only (~0.5 W per 64 GB RDIMM); the /32-48 comes from N-63's ECC-stretched interval, compaction gives 2-3x. Adds no bits; ~16 s break-even.
decisive_experiment: None needed: a zram-plus-PASR measurement on an LPDDR5 phone board would confirm the known 2-3x idle refresh saving within a week.
prior_art: LPDDR PASR; RAMZzz (SC 2012) migrates pages to power down ranks; GreenDIMM (MICRO 2021); Android zram and compaction. From memory.

key_insight: Compression frees in-slot room for t=7 BCH at zero capacity cost; at 1e-4 raw BER a ~512-bit codeword fails <1e-15, so compressible rows tolerate 0.5-1 s refresh.
killer_doubt: Inference now stores FP8/FP4 weights and KV, compressing <10-15% against the 15.6% needed to fit 54 B; the BF16-era 44 B figure fails, so fully compressible rows are rare.
decisive_experiment: Dump real HBM contents (FP8/FP4 weights, KV) from vLLM runs and measure the share of 8 KB rows fully <=54 B; FPGA DDR5 BER at 0.5-1 s, 85 C to confirm a <=2e-4 tail.
prior_art: COP compress-and-protect (Palframan et al., ISCA 2015); Hi-ECC 1 s refresh (Wilkerson et al., ISCA 2010); MECC morphable ECC. From memory.

key_insight: Retention is bought by temperature: capacity DRAM on 35 C sleds could refresh 4-18x less, or a cool-spec die could use a ~30% shorter capacitor.
killer_doubt: Tail cells (GIDL, trap-assisted) have low Ea, so tail retention may gain only 3-5x; LPDDR temperature-compensated refresh already harvests this, worth ~10% of DRAM power. HBM cannot leave the GPU.
decisive_experiment: FPGA DRAM tester on a thermal chuck: measure 1e-6-quantile retention of 1b DDR5 dies at 35, 55 and 85 C to fix tail Ea; about one month and ~$50k.
prior_art: LPDDR4/5 temperature-controlled refresh (MR4); DDR4/5 2x refresh above 85 C; liquid-cooled DIMMs in HPC; C0 N-42. From memory.

key_insight: For iid defects the arithmetic holds: t=2 BCH on 144-bit words at p=1e-4 leaves ~62 three-defect words per 16 Gb die, remappable in a small CAM.
killer_doubt: Patterning defects cluster (one particle kills 1e2-1e4 cells), not iid at 1e-4 (1e7/cm2); ~12,500 two-defect words per die keep zero soft-error margin. DDR5 on-die ECC exists.
decisive_experiment: Analysis only (<$100k): take fail-bit maps from a DSA or NIL line-array test vehicle, fit spatial clustering, and compare yield under word-level BCH versus mat sparing.
prior_art: DDR5 on-die SEC (128+8), HBM ECC, NAND bad-block management, row/column redundancy; C0 rated N-34 KNOWN+TWIST. From memory.

key_insight: SA offset is static, so row-wise codewords make offset errors near-iid; t=8 BCH at 1e-4 raw BER fails ~2e-17 per read, halving capacitor height (AR 62 to 30).
killer_doubt: Row-correlated errors share one codeword: half-margin cells may flip at ~2x fewer hammer activations (~500); a 13 fA tail cell droops 0.31 of 0.5 V in 64 ms.
decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender/SoftMC on DDR5: emulate half charge with truncated tRAS restore; map BER versus margin, temperature and hammer count; test whether errors along rows are iid. ~$100k, six months.
prior_art: Hi-ECC (Wilkerson et al., ISCA 2010); DDR5 on-die ECC; NAND soft-decision LDPC; approximate DRAM. Capacitor redesigned around ECC margin: none found.

key_insight: Read disturb, not write endurance, is HBF's real wear-out for inference; per-block read-rate arithmetic must enter any HBF dossier.
killer_doubt: Disturb counts per block: 1.6 TB/s over 512 GB gives each ~500-page pSLC block ~1.3e8 reads/day; a ~1e6 limit forces ~130 rewrites/day, ~2.4e5 P/E in 5 years.
decisive_experiment: Raw 2xx-layer 3D NAND on an ONFI tester (~$50k): apply 1e7-1e9 block reads in pSLC mode at 55-85 C and track RBER growth to set the true reclaim interval.
prior_art: SanDisk and SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash (2025-26); SSD read-disturb counters and relocation are standard FTL practice. From memory.

key_insight: Continuous BEOL wires around folds replace TSVs, bumps and alignment; a dead die is bypassed by its pass-through wiring, so spare layers restore stack yield without known-good-die.
killer_doubt: Layer pitch is ~2x fold radius (300-600 um at r=150-300 um), far above HBM's ~45 um; even 67 um pitch leaves 16 adhesive layers at ~30 K/W over 100 mm2.
decisive_experiment: Cu/polyimide daisy-chain membrane of 4 die images (0.5-2 um lines) on glass; laser release, fold at r=33-300 um; measure line yield, resistance after 1,000 thermal cycles and stack thermal resistance with Si-foil interleaves.
prior_art: Folded-flex stacked packages (Tessera micro-Z fold; Intel folded stacked CSP, ~2002). Monolithic BEOL fold-wired memory stack: none found. Unverified.
